turns.text: Hello, come in. How have you been since last time?
The journey here took a while, but at least I had time to gather my thoughts.
Tell me more about that.
I finally told Claire about the panic attack on the train and she hugged me and cried.
I see. Can you say a bit more?
The train was late again this morning, so I almost did not make it on time today. That is how it was.
And how was that for you?
I am not sure where to begin, there are so many things going round in my head at the moment.
What went through your mind then?
My GP prescribed sertraline, fifty milligrams, and I am nervous about the side effects.
And how was that for you?
It is strange to sit here and say all of this out loud, but it does help a little. I keep coming back to it.
Take your time.
Hannah called and said she will fly over from Toronto in March for two weeks to help with Dad.
Take your time.
I made myself a cup of tea this morning and just stood by the window for a while. It is not easy to talk about.
Take your time.
I had a long day yesterday and I was so tired in the evening that I just sat in front of the television.
What happened next?
I really miss running on Saturdays, my legs feel restless and heavy.
How did that feel for you?
Some days are better than others, and I try to remind myself of that when things get heavy. I keep coming back to it.
Let us stop here for today.
Thank you, see you next week.
